newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan prosecutors indict Nomura as a company.
newsitem.headline: Japan prosecutors indict Nomura as a company.

text.p: Tokyo Prosecutors on Wednesday for the first time directly linked Nomura Securities Co Ltd itself to a scandal involving illegal payoffs to corporate racketeers.

A statement by the prosecutors office said Japan's biggest brokerage had been indicted as a company for violation of securities law by illegally compensating for trading losses a firm owned by the brother of a racketeer.

The statement said two former Nomura directors were also indicted for giving 49.7 million yen ($428,000) to racketeer Ryuichi Koike through his brother's firm in March 1995 in violation of Japan's securities and exchange law and the commercial code.

Shimpei Matsuki, chief of Nomura's equity department and Nobutaka Fujikura, head of the general affairs department, were indicted for conspiring with other Nomura officials to give cash to racketeers to stop them from disrupting shareholder meetings.

The scandal first surfaced in early May when Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), filed a complaint with prosecutors against Nomura, the two executives and a company official.

Although prosecutors have also arrested ex-Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki, the company has maintained the scandal involved actions of individuals, not the corporation itself. Distinction between corporate and individual responsibility is a key factor in deciding punishment for breaches of securities law. ($1=116 yen)
